headline: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has called for direct talks with North Korea to formally end the Korean War, seeking to replace the 73-year-old armistice with a permanent peace agreement. From my understanding, North Korea previously pursued unification with the South. However, after Kim Jong Un abandoned that policy and began treating South Korea as a separate, hostile state, it seems that the options for a peaceful settlement have become much more limited. A permanent peace agreement could also be difficult for Pyongyang to accept, as it could imply recognition of South Korea as a legitimate, separate state.

headline: The U.S. Missile Defense Agency (MDA) has issued a pre-solicitation notice for a new mobile radar designed to detect and track ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missiles. The MDA is seeking a prototype and plans to use accelerated contracting authorities to move the program forward. The effort comes as the U.S. seeks to improve its ability to detect and track increasingly advanced missile threats from China, Russia and Iran, including hypersonic weapons. The new radar would build on the role currently performed by the AN/TPY-2 Forward-Based Mode radar, which is already part of the U.S. ballistic missile defense architecture.

headline: More than 1,300 Strava users have publicly logged workouts from U.S. military sites across the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) area, according to an investigation by Sky News cited by Task & Purpose. The exposure is particularly concerning because many of these installations have subsequently been targeted by Iran. At Muwaffaq Al Salti Air Base in Jordan, for example, personnel regularly posted runs around the installation. Activity resumed in April and later became concentrated around barracks; the housing area was struck in July, killing three U.S. soldiers. The issue isn't new. In 2018, Strava's public heat maps exposed previously undisclosed military locations and details about base layouts. The Pentagon subsequently prohibited personnel from using geolocation features on personal or government devices. CENTCOM has since issued additional OPSEC guidance, including restrictions implemented when Operation Epic Fury began. Yet publicly available Strava data shows personnel are still exposing their locations. This is particularly notable given Adm. Brad Cooper's warning last month that Iran was using troops' photos, videos and other cellphone-generated information to assess strike effectiveness and help target U.S. personnel. Below are screenshots taken from the Strava app today showing activity at Muwaffaq Al Salti Air Base, Jordan and Prince Sultan Air Base, Saudi Arabia. The blue lines are tracks uploaded to the app by users with the darker color representing higher usage of route.

headline: The U.S. Navy is considering a major redesign of its new Ford-class aircraft carriers to better match President Trump’s preferred aesthetic for the warships, according to seven current and former U.S. officials familiar with the matter who spoke to the Washington Post. The President has expressed concerns over the location of the “island” on the Ford-class of carriers, which operates as the ship’s bridge as well as an air traffic control tower and is located more towards the rear of the vessel, with Trump preferring the multistory tower be moved to the middle of the flight deck, like on aircraft carriers seen during World War ll. Moving that command center would be the second major design change prompted by President Trump, who on Thursday issued a national security memorandum directing the Navy to develop a plan to revert to older steam-powered catapults on future aircraft carriers, scrapping the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS) currently employed on the USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78).

headline: The Arleigh Burke class guided missile destroyer USS Benfold (DDG-65) suffered an engineering casualty affecting its power-generation system on July 24 while conducting routine operations in the South China Sea with the USS George Washington (CVN-73) Carrier Strike Group. The casualty resulted in a complete loss of power for four days, during which the George Washington Carrier Strike Group provided essential support to the destroyer, including meals, until Benfold was able to reach Subic Bay, Philippines, for repairs. During the outage, the Benfold had limited potable water and no galley, restrooms and climate control. Benfold subsequently returned to its homeport of Yokosuka, Japan, on August 12, as seen in imagery from @Gov_Vessel_fan.

headline: The extended deployment of USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) and reported supply problems appear to be tied in part to the loss of the Navy’s logistics hub in Bahrain early in the Iran war according to a report from the New York Times. Iranian missile and drone strikes heavily damaged the Naval Support Activity Bahrain, home of the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet, forcing the Navy to shift much of its regional logistics support to Naval Support Facility Diego Garcia, roughly 2,200 miles from the carrier forces operating in the Gulf of Oman. The island subsequently became an Iranian target, with two ballistic missiles launched toward Diego Garcia on March 20; one fell short and a Navy ship intercepted the other. That logistical disruption has coincided with an unusually demanding deployment for Lincoln. The carrier has been at sea for nearly nine months without a liberty call, while supporting combat operations and the blockade of Iranian ports. Lawmakers have raised concerns about reported shortages of basic supplies and deteriorating crew morale. The Navy is now replacing Lincoln with the forward deployed USS George Washington (CVN-73), which is already transiting toward the Middle East. Another carrier, George H.W. Bush, has also been operating in the region for months.
